text:
Dear Partners,

It was, by all accounts, a quiet session on the wire this quarter, and the data prints came in line with expectation — the kind of unremarkable stretch that we at Stonebeck Credit have come to treasure, the way a farmer treasures a stretch of ordinary weather between the planting and the harvest. Nothing dramatic grew, but nothing was lost to frost either. The central bank held its policy rate at 5.00%, inflation sits at 2.9%, and high-yield spreads at 400bps continue to tell a market story of caution without alarm. We take comfort in the calm, though we've learned — as any lender who has sat across the table from a borrower through a cycle learns — that quiet quarters are not proof against loud ones.

On the portfolio: we are pleased to report a quarter of +1.1%, bringing year-to-date to +1.1% as well, and since inception to +33.0% — a figure we remain proud of, and one we believe reflects the discipline of structural seniority in every position we hold. Our NAV index sits at 101.1, steady and unspectacular in the best sense of the word.

We know some of you will note that public equities returned +1.3% this quarter, a gap worth naming rather than dancing around. We don't chase that comparison, and we'd ask you not to either. Ours is a different partnership — one built on cash flows we can see, collateral we can touch, and structural seniority that stands ahead of the equity cushion in every capital stack we lend into. Public markets price hope and headlines by the hour; we price contracts, covenants, and the discipline of a lender who intends to be repaid. The gap will open and close with sentiment; our job is to keep the underlying credit sound regardless of which way the wind is blowing on any given Tuesday.

As for what's ahead — we remain constructive, though not complacent. Spreads at 400bps still compensate patient capital fairly, and CPI at 2.9% suggests the policy path may stay steadier than markets feared a year ago. Still, we'd be poor stewards if we didn't watch for the moment sentiment turns, as it always eventually does. Should conditions tighten meaningfully, we believe our structural seniority and the relationships — genuine partnerships — we've built with our borrowers position us to work through it constructively, as we always have. We remain prudent about the pace of new commitments and continue to believe recovery is likely wherever stress does emerge, though no lender can ever predict the weather.

As always, we thank our limited partners for their continued trust.

Warmly,

R. Okafor
On behalf of Stonebeck Credit
